checks.assessment: Water vapor is distinguished from liquid droplets; evaporation/condensation are opposite phase changes. The dilute-mixture model keeps temperature and volume unchanged when explaining partial pressure. Saturation is described through balance with same-temperature liquid water with continuing molecular exchange, and unsaturation through lower vapor pressure, not physically full air. Relative humidity retains its same-temperature comparison.

Graph orientation and A-to-B cooling preserve constant water-vapor partial pressure, unchanged gas proportions and approximately constant total pressure before condensation. Temperature below B is the dew point. Dewpoint tables provide original actual pressure, which is compared to saturation pressure at original air temperature, not the dew point a second time. Fog/dew remain distinct and conditionally formed.

G is separated from the thermometer sensing bulb, C is explicitly a modern polished-face label, and surface/thermometer temperature correspondence remains required. Hair calibration and gauze are explained. Net evaporation means more molecules leave than return; at same-temperature equilibrium they exchange at equal overall rates and net evaporative cooling vanishes. Appropriate pressure, air movement and instrument/table conditions remain. No ether operating instructions or arbitrary numeric readings are added.

Heat-term meanings, mass fractions, signs and heat-balance algebra remain coherent. Added L and c explanations have correct dimensions. Average starting temperature plus0.1L/(2c) gives about55+27.38=82.38 C, consistent with the retained rounded82 C result and complete condensation under the stated no-loss model.

Kelvin is correctly distinguished from Celsius, the approximate273 offset leads to about420 K, and R about8.31 with SI units is appropriate. Molar mass is per mole, not per molecule. Numerator/divisor explanation gives final ideal-vapor volume about0.22 m3; subtracting0.5 m3 gives approximately-0.28 m3, rounded to-0.3 m3. Fixed mass, constant147 C, corrected4.4e5 Pa and real-vapor approximation limits remain.
